item.title: CAS review: Sebi announces last 30-minute VWAP method for settlement
item.description: Sebi has revised the closing auction session framework, adopting the last 30-minute VWAP for derivatives settlement and changing trading hours from December 7, 2026.
item.dc:creator: Khushboo Tiwari
item.content:encoded: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) on Thursday announced the much-awaited revisions to the closing auction session (CAS) framework, introducing changes to the settlement methodology, trading timings, and the transition of unexecuted iceberg orders. An iceberg order is a large order split into smaller orders where only a fraction of the total quantity is visible in the order book displayed to the public. The revised framework will take effect from December 7, 2026, except for changes relating to the transition of unexecuted limit and iceberg orders from the continuous trading session (CTS) to CAS, which will come into force from February 8, 2027. Retaining the earlier method, the settlement price of index derivatives will be based on the volume-weighted average prices (VWAP) of constituent securities during the last 30 minutes of the CTS (3.00 pm to 3.30 pm) in the equity cash segment.For expiring stock derivatives, clearing corporations will determine settlement prices using the VWAP of the underlying stock during the last 30 minutes of the CTS across all stock exchanges. Exchanges will provide the VWAP and quantity traded to clearing corporations and continuously disseminate indicative values to market participants in real time during this period. Under the revised timings, CAS will operate as a separate 10-minute session from 3:30 pm to 3:40 pm on all trading days. The order-entry period will close randomly between 3:38 pm and 3:40 pm. Trading in index derivatives will continue until 3:45 pm on regular trading days, but contracts expiring that day will stop trading at 3:30 pm. Trading in stock derivatives will continue until 3:45 pm, including on expiry days. The post-close session in the cash segment will run from 3:50 pm to 4 pm, with trades executed at the closing prices of securities. CAS became effective on August 3 and saw an uproar from the trading community over the settlement price, sharp spikes, and low liquidity. The latest changes were announced following a consultation paper that received over 20,000 suggestions, which was followed by deliberations of the market regulator’s Secondary Market Advisory Committee on Thursday. The regulator had also proposed a blended mechanism, on which several market participants had raised concerns, given the low liquidity in the window.  Traders and brokers had favoured the 30-minute VWAP method stating that participants were more familiar with this mechanism and that it was more transparent and operationally well understood. On Thursday, Sebi also specified how unexecuted orders will move from the CTS to CAS. Pending limit orders will generally be carried forward, except stop-loss orders and orders priced beyond the applicable CAS price bands. Unexecuted iceberg orders within the applicable price bands will be converted into fully disclosed limit orders (at fixed/pre-determined price), unless market participants opt out when placing the original orders. These converted orders will have lower time priority than other limit orders carried forward from the continuous session, but higher priority than limit orders placed during CAS. At present, CAS is a 20 minute window from 3:15 pm to 3:35 pm where the reference price calculation and transition from CTS to CAS happens from 3:15 pm to 3:20 pm. In this period, no order entry is allowed. The next five minutes order entry period remains. From 3.25 pm to 3.30 pm, the order entry period is restricted to limit orders only, and no modifications or cancellations of market orders are allowed. In this period, trading closes randomly in the last two minutes. In its consultation paper, Sebi had also proposed prohibiting cancellation of limit orders placed beyond 1 per cent range of the reference price during CAS. However, the regulator skipped this change in the final circular. What’s new Stock derivatives’ settlement prices will use underlying stocks’ volume-weighted average prices across exchangesCAS will run from 3:30 pm to 3:40 pm, with random closureExpiring index derivatives will stop trading at 3:30 pm; stock derivatives at 3:45 pmIceberg orders will become fully disclosed limit orders unless participants opt out

item.title: India-US trade deal: 'Big items done', both sides close to pact, says Gor
item.description: US envoy Sergio Gor expresses confidence in finalising the India-US trade deal, saying key issues have been resolved ...
item.content:encoded:
Home / World News / India-US trade deal: 'Big items done', both sides close to pact, says Gor

India-US trade deal: 'Big items done', both sides close to pact, says Gor US envoy Sergio Gor expresses confidence in finalising the India-US trade deal, saying key issues have been resolved

US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor | Image: Bloomberg

Press Trust of India New Delhi 5 min read Last Updated : Oct 15 2026 | 11:54 PM IST

Listen to This Article

US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor on Thursday said negotiations for a bilateral trade deal were moving at an "incredible pace", and the "big items are done", underlining that he was confident that both sides will get the pact through. During an interactive session at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum here, Gor also echoed External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar's assessment of the progress in the proposed India-US trade pact, saying "we are very close to landing it". Asked about the status of the negotiations, Gor said, "I won't like to get into too many details at this stage, and let the ministers announce that. But in the grand scheme of things, big items are done."   "We're actively engaged... Within three weeks of arriving here, we announced a trade deal. The European Union trade deal took almost 20 years. So we're at an incredible pace, and I am confident that we will get it done," Gor said.

The India-EU Free Trade Agreement (FTA) was successfully concluded in January after nearly 20 years of negotiation. "We have been at it for a year-and-a-half. We are at an incredible pace, I would say almost an unheard of pace So I am confident that we will get it (the deal) done," Gor said. Also Read

First tranche of India-US deal close to conclusion, says Piyush Goyal

US trade pact to be operationalised once India gets competitive edge: Goyal

Closer trade ties with India remain top priority: US envoy Sergio Gor

Rubio to visit Jamnagar, Mumbai as US trade deal near 'landing point'

Can India's latest FTAs put it on the road to Viksit Atmanirbhar Bharat? premium

India has maintained that both sides remain engaged for a mutually beneficial bilateral trade agreement. The two sides continue to engage to iron out differences on the proposed deal, and negotiations are heading towards a "landing point", Jaishankar had said at an earlier session at the Forum, noting that the core fundamentals of the bilateral strategic partnership remained unchanged.

Gor said, "We are getting there. I am confident that we will have a trade deal here, as you heard Dr Jaishankar say right on this stage, and we are very close to landing it."   He was also asked about the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, and if there is any room for some sanctions relief or exemptions related to it for India. "That is a decision for the president," Gor said, adding the legislation gives the US president that authority. He has not imposed sanctions on any country yet. The bill was passed recently, and "he has to make a determination within the next 10 days or so, and I am sure we will see an announcement from the White House soon," Gor said.

On September 18, US President Donald Trump signed into law the 'Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026', which authorises him to impose tariffs of up to 100 per cent on countries buying Russian oil and gas, including China and India. Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri, during his meeting with a bipartisan US Congressional delegation in Delhi, had conveyed India's "concerns" over the implications of the recently enacted Act on bilateral ties and the international energy market. The US envoy also underlined that this was a "very complex trade deal". A lot of smaller countries do not have "tens of thousands of points to figure out", he said.

"You are always going to have something, some small items New items develop constantly, new technology comes up, new issues arise, which is natural. A country like India with 1.4 billion people is a complex place, and so matching everything won't be done overnight. But the big picture, the big framework, the big items are done," the envoy said. Gor's comments assume significance, as they come a few days ahead of US Secretary of State Marco Rubio's upcoming visit to India. The envoy also referred to a US Supreme Court ruling related to the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA). "The Supreme Court had ruled that law unconstitutional, so the administration had to go back and rework some of those," he said.

The comment was made in the context of the complexities involved in the proposed trade deal. Gor also said that US Trade Representative (USTR) Jamieson Greer and India's Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal are literally discussing the proposed trade deal down to smaller details. "You have an unmatched market here for our companies You have 1.4 billion people. And American products are popular in India. The NBA (National Basketball Association, a professional basketball league in the US) has got a following here, and you don't even have a league yet. "So, for the private sector to be able to come to India to compete, to have their foot in the door, you have a very pragmatic prime minister... That welcomes outside investment," Gor said.

"Pick any sector, and we're working together at it. If you look at defence, we have co-production happening here in India. If you look at IT, it's unmatched. Google, Microsoft, Adobe, Micron -- each one of them is opening data centres and chip manufacturing units here that work with our companies, hand in hand, in the US. "So when a job is created in India, a counter job is created in the US. It is an incredible win-win situation that I would call unmatched. Not a lot of countries in the world have such limitless potential," he said.

(Only the headline and picture of this report may have been reworked by the Business Standard staff; the rest of the content is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)

item.content:encoded:
Home / Companies / News / AstraZeneca strikes $40 million AI drug discovery deal with Insitro

AstraZeneca strikes $40 million AI drug discovery deal with Insitro The multi-year partnership will target severe liver and heart conditions, with insitro eligible for up to $1.46 billion in development and commercial milestone payments

AstraZeneca has partnered with AI biotech firm insitro to discover treatments for severe liver and heart conditions.

Reuters 2 min read Last Updated : Oct 15 2026 | 9:47 PM IST

Listen to This Article

AstraZeneca has teamed up with artificial intelligence biotech company insitro to discover and develop new treatments for difficult to treat liver and heart conditions, the British drugmaker said on Thursday.   Under the agreement, AstraZeneca will pay $40 million up front, with California-based insitro eligible for up to about $1.46 billion in potential development and commercial milestones, as well as a single-digit percentage of future sales in royalties.   The multi-year collaboration will focus on metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), a severe liver disease, and cardiomyopathies, a group of diseases that affect the heart muscle. Both have historically lacked effective therapies because researchers have struggled to pinpoint their root biological drivers, the drugmaker said.

Insitro will use its "Virtual Human" AI platform, which combines lab-grown cell models and machine learning, to identify causal disease biology and advance AstraZeneca-nominated targets from discovery to development-candidate stage. AstraZeneca will then run and fund future clinical trials.   The deal builds on insitro's expansion across the pharmaceuticals industry. The biotech company recently expanded its partnership with Bristol Myers Squibb to advance a broader portfolio of targets for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). It also teamed up with Eli Lilly to build AI models that predict pharmacological properties of small molecules â in living organisms.   "Choosing the new targets that we want to put into our discovery pipeline is one of the hardest things we do across research and development," Sharon Barr, executive vice president of biopharmaceuticals R&D at AstraZeneca, told Reuters.

"By the time we read about a new pathway or target (in major scientific journals), it is no longer novel. It's in the public domain and we're already a few steps too late. But when we identify these unique connections early and test them in cellular systems, we're ahead of the game." Barr added that pairing AI tools with experienced scientists allows the company to test fewer molecules in the lab, reduce guesswork and speed the search for effective medicines.     More From This Section

item.title: Google DeepMind ties up with ICRISAT to develop plant genome atlas
item.description: The open-access catalogue will use AI to help breeders identify promising plant combinations faster, while the partnership will also support genome mapping for other crops ...
item.dc:creator: Aashish Aryan
item.content:encoded: Google DeepMind and Google.org have partnered with Hyderabad-headquartered International Crops Research Institute for the Semi-Arid Tropics (ICRISAT) to launch an open-access global public genetic atlas aimed at identifying the most promising plant combinations, particularly in sorghum, Google India said. “The resulting AI-supported genetic catalogue is aimed at helping breeders and researchers across the world to develop more resilient and productive sorghum varieties faster than traditional methods, which can involve decade-long trial-and-error processes,” the company said in a blog post. Google DeepMind will also support a three-year postdoctoral fellowship at ICRISAT to help develop tools that can map and characterise genomes for other crops and pulses such as chickpea, groundnut and pigeon pea, the company said. “We aim for this collaboration to unlock the global potential of indigenous climate-resilient crops like sorghum, and to empower the agri ecosystem with cutting-edge tools that strengthen global food security and safeguard present and future generations,” Stanford Blade, deputy director general of research and innovation at ICRISAT, said. Separately, Google is expanding access to its Agricultural Understanding Models to enable developers, startups and researchers to build customised solutions for hyperlocal farming challenges and strengthen agricultural resilience, the company said. The move is aimed at widening access to AI tools that can be used to address local agricultural conditions and improve decision-making across the farm ecosystem. Google’s AI Educator Series, first launched in May this year in partnership with five states, is now being expanded to Bihar and Madhya Pradesh. The series will also be made available as a free online resource accessible to users across the country, Google India said. Google.org, Google’s philanthropic arm, will also provide $15 million to The/Nudge to support the growth of micro, small and medium enterprises in India. “This initiative will fund the development of scalable AI tools to expand small enterprises' access to formal credit, market discovery, and compliance,” the company said.
